title: GitHub Pages and Documentation Automation practice
prompt: Design a docs build and link-check pipeline with a preview stage and a controlled publishing gate.
objective: Demonstrate the behavior of github pages and documentation automation practice and capture verifiable evidence.

starter.code:
name: Build and publish GitHub Pages
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: echo "Build your documentation site into ./dist"
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: ./dist
  deploy:
    needs: build
    permissions:
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    environment:
      name: github-pages
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

expected_output: A reviewed workflow or design note satisfying: link, build, publish. Verify behavior on a disposable repository where execution is required; a static sketch is not proof of a live deployment.
acceptance_criteria: Explain one validation result or limitation.
Do not include a real secret or use production resources.
hints: First identify the trigger, input, and expected result.
Start with read-only permissions and a disposable branch or test environment.
Compare your result with the linked lesson and official documentation; distinguish a configuration sketch from a live integration.

solution.explanation: The detailed reference solution is stored in a protected repository-only JSON file; it is not intended for a learner-facing response.

grading_method: Server-side required-string smoke check plus human review for workflow semantics and security boundaries.
retry_policy: Allow retries; incorrect submissions do not award XP. The platform awards exercise XP only after server-verified successful completion and applies idempotency per activity.
